chunks: Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, is referring to the death of the Messenger of Allāh, peace be upon him and his descendants.

key_terms.السَّيِّدُ الرِّضْيُ: As-Sayyid ar-Raḍī, a prominent Shia scholar and compiler of Nahj al-Balagha
key_terms.صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ: Peace be upon him and his family

ai.seo_question: What does As-Sayyid ar-Raḍī mean by 'referring to the death of the Messenger of Allah' in this context?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Radi clarifies that the context refers specifically to the death of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), anchoring the verse in the pivotal event of the Prophet's passing. This exegetical note highlights the profound grief associated with the loss of the Imam of Guidance, a central theme in Shia hermeneutics for understanding verses related to mourning and spiritual transition.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, is referring to the death of the Messenger of Allāh, peace be upon him and his descendants.
